summary: This bill creates a National Infrastructure Bank as a government corporation that raises up to $500 billion in capital by swapping long-term Treasury bonds and municipal bonds for non-voting preferred shares paying Treasury-rate dividends, accepts deposits, issues bonds, and provides up to $5 trillion in loans and guarantees to governments and private entities for building or upgrading roads, bridges, energy systems, water facilities, broadband, affordable housing, and other infrastructure projects selected for job creation, economic growth, and environmental benefits.

scores.thoughts: The bill establishes a National Infrastructure Bank as a government corporation authorized to issue up to $500B in capital stock (with Treasury subscribing up to $100B) and make up to $5T in loans for infrastructure, backed by full faith and credit. It requires only $50M initial appropriations but creates massive lending capacity with contingent Treasury liability. Findings emphasize closing a $3.7T+ infrastructure gap through this mechanism without new taxes/deficits, but it expands government financing role significantly, effectively increasing government involvement in economy via credit extension for public projects. This strongly pushes toward expanding government spending/financing.

Title I provides tax exemptions: Bank treated as 501(l) exempt corporation; contributions deductible as charitable under 170(c); preferred dividends excludible from gross income under new 139J. These are targeted tax incentives to capitalize/attract funds to the Bank, reducing tax burdens for contributors/investors. Not broad tax cuts, but clear tax relief to enable the Bank's operations. Medium impact toward lower taxes.
No mention of healthcare, insurance, providers, or related policies. Zero bearing.
No provisions related to guns, rights, or regulations. Zero bearing.
No references to immigration, borders, pathways, or protections. Zero bearing.
No mention of abortion or reproductive rights. Zero bearing.
No provisions on military spending, defense budget, or related. Zero bearing.

Eligibility criteria prioritize projects with environmental benefits (GHG reduction, pollution cuts, resiliency, wetlands, clean energy retrofits, smart grid). Includes environmental infrastructure (water, waste, flood control). Promotes 'energy savings' and domestic clean production. Tangentially expands environmental protections via financed projects, but not regulatory; financing mechanism.

Funds affordable housing and disadvantaged communities as infrastructure, but not welfare, food stamps, or direct aid programs. Focus is job creation/productivity, not expanding entitlements. No bearing on core safety net.
Infrastructure includes schools (repair/expansion) and broadband access. Workforce training facilities mentioned. Minor implications for public school investment via financing.
No drug-related provisions. Zero bearing.
Local hiring preferences prioritize ex-offenders (barriers to employment). Very tangential to reform/rehab.

Requires Buy America compliance; stimulates domestic production of materials if insufficient; prioritizes projects promoting domestic construction inputs. Protectionist elements to boost US manufacturing.

Claims to finance without new taxes/deficits via self-sustaining bank (exchanged securities, deposits, bonds). But Treasury on-call $100B subscription, contingent liability for losses, massive $5T lending backed by US credit. Findings accept investment needs over strict debt reduction; initial $50M auth. Moderately accepts deficit spending for investment via off-budget lending.
Nondiscrimination policy explicitly includes 'sexual orientation, gender identity' for Bank employment/projects. Minor expansion of protections.
No foreign aid provisions. Domestic focus only. Zero bearing.
No election or voting-related content. Zero bearing.
Funds telecom/broadband infrastructure, AI/network security enhancements. No privacy regs or oversight. Tangential to less regulation on tech.

Strong pro-labor: Davis-Bacon prevailing wages; project labor agreements required/encouraged; union reps (AFL-CIO, Building Trades) on Board; apprenticeships; local hiring with unions. Prioritizes worker protections/union rights.

Broad nondiscrimination (race, religion, sex, etc.) for employment/projects, prioritizing civil rights compliance (Civil Rights Act). No religious exemptions mentioned. Minor toward civil rights over exemptions.
